---
title: "The Shape of Conflict: Detecting and Quantifying Impulse-Decay Mortality Signatures in Civil Conflicts Using All-Cause Mortality Surfaces"
author:
  - name: Jonathan Minton
    orcid: 0000-0003-1207-6259
    email: nate.minton@gmail.com
    corresponding: true
date: last-modified
abstract: |
  Conflict demography faces a data paradox: the populations most affected by civil
  conflict tend to have the weakest mortality data. We propose a method for detecting
  and quantifying conflict-attributable excess mortality using only all-cause mortality
  data by age, sex, and year. Building on the insight that mortality surfaces are
  fundamentally smooth spatial objects, we develop a Bayesian framework that identifies
  structured departures from smoothness consistent with an impulse-decay conflict
  process --- a sharp onset of excess mortality in young adult males followed by
  exponential decay over years or decades. The model jointly estimates onset timing,
  decay rate, and age-specific magnitude, with uncertainty propagated to excess death
  estimates. Applied to Northern Ireland (the Troubles, half-life ~7 years) and Algeria
  (the Black Decade, half-life ~3 years), the model captures 75% of independently
  tallied conflict deaths from all-cause data alone. A systematic scan of all Human
  Mortality Database countries tests the method's specificity and sensitivity. The
  decay rate characterises conflict dynamics: longer half-lives suggest entrenched
  tit-for-tat processes; shorter half-lives suggest more acute phases. This
  lightweight approach extends conflict mortality estimation to settings where
  detailed cause-of-death data are unavailable.
keywords:
  - Conflict demography
  - Mortality surfaces
  - Lexis surface
  - Bayesian model comparison
  - Impulse-decay model
  - Northern Ireland
  - Civil conflict
---
